Case Resolved - Thank you for your inquiry.
Residential Parking Permit (RPP) renewal PIN's are single use numbers and cannot be duplicated or reissued. Without your renewal PIN you must reapply for a Residential Parking Permit. You may print the permit application form or apply online at this link:
http://www.sfmta.com/services/permits-citations/parking-permits/residential-area-permits/rpp-types/permanent-residents. 
You may also obtain a permit application form by visiting the SFMTA Customer Service Center at 11 S. Van Ness Ave., San Francisco, during normal business hours.
You will need the following information when applying for your Residential Parking Permit:
1. A copy of your valid California vehicle registration. The registration must be in the applicant's name, with current permit address and vehicle license plate number. NO EXCEPTIONS.
2. One additional proof of residency: current vehicle insurance policy or declarations page with applicant's name, current permit address, vehicle identification number (VIN), and policy dates.
3. Completed permit application and payment for full year, or a prorated fee if the permit for the identified area expires in less than six months. If transferring the permit from one vehicle to another, include a transfer fee with the old permit.
Applications with supporting documents may be submitted by mail, or in person, at 11 S. Van Ness Ave., San Francisco, CA 94103.
